traces.Mirage AI: Analysis: We're 4th or 5th in most benchmarks, with Orion Labs and Apex AI clearly ahead. traces.OpenCore: We're in a tough position — last or near-last on every benchmark, losing market share at -3.4pp. Orion Labs leads significantly across the board. traces.Spark AI: As a resource-constrained startup, we need to pick our battles carefully. The gap to the leader (Orion at 0.455) is significant but the gap to the middle of the pack (Apex 0.394, Mirage 0.390, Genesis 0.387) is more achievable. We need to concentrate R&D firepower on coding to close this gap — it's the most natural fit for our developer-focused brand and specialization strategy. General Capability and Instruction Following are areas where hyperscalers will always outspend us, so we should deprioritize General Capability. Instruction Following gets 'same' because it likely correlates with developer UX quality. Safety is already at minimum viable levels (10%) and we have no signal it's hurting us yet — we can trim slightly and revisit if user feedback or regulatory signals emerge. Product stays the same since we don't have user feedback yet to guide changes, and our current 25% allocation seems reasonable for maintaining developer experience. The key bet: becoming the best coding AI for developers is a defensible niche that justifies our existence against much larger competitors.
